title: The Hidden Life of Embeddings: Linus Lee

primary.label: Model Foundations & Behavior

summary: Linus Lee opens with his motivation: steering language models via prompts alone feels indirect, like steering a car from the back seat with a pool noodle. He proposes looking inside models at latent spaces—high-dimensional vectors in embedding models, activation spaces, token embeddings, and autoencoders—as a way to gain more direct control. Embeddings theoretically encode the most salient features of input text, and disentangling these could enable more expressive interfaces for controlling models. He demonstrates an encoder-decoder model trained on a sentence about Greg Ean's novel Diaspora, producing a 248-dimensional embedding. The decoder reconstructs the original text, including specific details like the book title. By blurring the embedding, the decoder produces semantically degraded text. He identifies meaningful directions in embedding space—a length direction that shortens text while preserving topic, and a negative sentiment direction—and uses a spatial canvas interface to explore variations interactively. He projects embeddings onto these directions to measure attributes like sentiment, topic, and vocabulary elaborateness, correctly identifying a ChatGPT-rewritten pessimistic version as further along the negative sentiment axis. He demonstrates embedding mixing—taking the first ~1000 dimensions from one 2000-dimensional embedding and the last ~1000 from another—producing decoded text that is a semantic blend. A linear adapter enables a decoder trained on his own embedding model to read from OpenAI's text-embedding-ada-002 embeddings, recovering surprising detail including the proper noun Diaspora and quoted-title structure. Extending to image space, he uses CLIP embeddings to interpolate between a photograph and a cartoon avatar of himself, producing a smooth transition. He performs embedding arithmetic on images—subtracting the vector for 'a photo of a smiling man' and adding 'a photo of a very sad crying man'—and combines style and subject simultaneously. He notes that all these manipulations involve only calculating embeddings and adding/subtracting vectors with normalization. He references groundbreaking research from Anthropic and Conjecture on unsupervised methods to automatically discover interpretable dimensions inside models. His text model is a custom encoder-decoder transformer fine-tuned from T5 with a special gated layer that decodes from embeddings. The image model is an unCLIP diffusion model trained to invert CLIP embeddings, similar to DALL-E 2. He announces these models are now open on Hugging Face with a Colab notebook. His core principle: when working with complex, inscrutable models, getting data into something tangible that can be seen, observed, and manipulated helps us understand and improve them. He closes with a Brett Victor quote: the purpose of a thinking medium is to bring thought outside the head, making the medium an extension of the mind.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

takeaways: Prompting language models has fundamental indirection; latent spaces offer a more direct control layer
Embeddings encode salient features that can be disentangled into meaningful directions such as length, sentiment, and topic
An encoder-decoder model can reconstruct text from embeddings and generate controlled variations by moving along semantic directions
Embedding mixing—slicing dimensions from different embeddings—produces semantic blends rather than gibberish
A linear adapter can enable a decoder trained on one embedding space to read from another (e.g., OpenAI Ada)
Embedding arithmetic extends to image space via CLIP, enabling interpolation and feature manipulation across modalities
All manipulations rely only on calculating embeddings and adding/subtracting vectors with normalization—no complex machinery
Models and Colab notebooks are openly released on Hugging Face for others to experiment with
Making model representations tangible and interactive is a core design principle for building better understanding and interfaces
Unsupervised methods from Anthropic and others are emerging to automatically discover interpretable dimensions inside models

sections.title: Introduction and Notion Context
sections.summary: Linus introduces himself as an AI engineer at Notion, previously an independent researcher working with embeddings, language models, and traditional NLP. Notion AI's public beta launched around November 2022 with features like AI autofill and translation. Notion is hiring AI engineers, product engineers, and ML engineers.

sections.title: Motivation: Latent Spaces and Model Control
sections.summary: Linus argues that prompting language models feels like steering a car from the back seat with a pool noodle—too many layers of indirection. He proposes looking inside models at latent spaces (embedding vectors, activation spaces, token embeddings, autoencoders) for more direct control. Embeddings pack salient features that could be disentangled to build more expressive interfaces for reading and intervening in model behavior.

sections.title: Encoder-Decoder Demo and Directional Manipulation
sections.summary: Demonstrates an encoder-decoder model on a sentence about Greg Egan's novel Diaspora, producing a 248-dimensional embedding. The decoder reconstructs the original text including the title. Blurring the embedding produces semantically degraded text. He identifies meaningful directions—a length direction that shortens text while preserving topic, and a negative sentiment direction—and uses a spatial canvas interface to explore variations interactively.

sections.title: Projecting Embeddings onto Meaningful Directions
sections.summary: Projects embeddings onto predefined directions to measure attributes like sentiment, artistic topic, length, and vocabulary elaborateness. Comparing the original neutral text with a ChatGPT-rewritten pessimistic version, the model correctly identifies the pessimistic version as further along the negative sentiment axis while other attributes remain roughly comparable.

sections.title: Embedding Mixing
sections.summary: Demonstrates mixing two 2000-dimensional embeddings by taking the first ~1000 dimensions from one and the last ~1000 from another. Despite the naive expectation of gibberish, the decoded result is a semantic blend sharing structural, topical, tonal, and punctuation similarities with both source texts.

sections.title: Cross-Embedding-Space Adapter
sections.summary: Shows that a decoder trained on his own embedding model can be adapted via a linear adapter to read from OpenAI's text-embedding-ada-002 embeddings. The adapted decoder recovers surprising detail from Ada embeddings alone, including the proper noun Diaspora, quoted-title structure, and roughly correct author name, though reconstruction is not as perfect as with the native model.

sections.title: Image Space Interpolation with CLIP
sections.summary: Extends embedding manipulation to image space using CLIP embeddings. Interpolates between a photograph of Linus and a cartoon Notion avatar version, generating six intermediate images showing a surprisingly smooth transition from photographic to cartoony features.

sections.title: Text-Based Image Manipulation via Embedding Arithmetic
sections.summary: Performs embedding arithmetic on images by subtracting the vector for 'a photo of a smiling man' and adding 'a photo of a very sad crying man,' requiring more careful scaling for text vectors. Also demonstrates combining style and subject simultaneously, smooth landscape transitions, and notes that all manipulations use only embedding calculation and vector addition with normalization. A beach addition did not survive the latent space arithmetic.

sections.title: Making Model Representations Visible and Research Context
sections.summary: Discusses the principle of rendering invisible model representations visible and directly interactive. References Anthropic's world model paper (neurons on a hack) and very recent work from Anthropic, Conjecture, and other labs on unsupervised methods to automatically discover interpretable dimensions inside models, complementing his manual centroid-based approach.

sections.title: Model Architecture and Open Release
sections.summary: Describes the text model as a custom encoder-decoder transformer fine-tuned from a T5 checkpoint with a special gated layer for decoding from embeddings. Explains the linear adapter training regime for cross-embedding-space decoding. Announces the models are now openly available on Hugging Face with a Colab notebook for quick experimentation with interpolation and interpretation.

sections.title: Image Model and Closing Philosophy
sections.summary: The image model is an unCLIP diffusion model trained to invert CLIP embeddings, similar to DALL-E 2. Linus's core takeaway: getting complex, inscrutable model data into something tangible that can be seen, observed, and manipulated deepens understanding and enables improvement. He closes with a Brett Victor quote: the purpose of a thinking medium is to bring thought outside the head, representing concepts in a form that can be seen with the senses and manipulated with the body, making the medium an extension of the mind.
